report.md:
## This week

You posted 11 videos this week. That's the same as last week. But views went down. Last week your typical video got about 2,300 views. This week your typical video got about 1,700 views. Your best video this week was the one that starts with "how it feels to be 23y old girly running a six figure business you started three months ago." That one pulled in 10,500 views. Your weakest video was the one with no real hook line, filmed talking to camera about everyday life, which only got 435 views. You've got two brand new videos that haven't had time to find their audience yet, so don't count those as wins or losses.

## Is it how you film, or what you say?

Right now, what you say seems to matter more than how you film it. You haven't given yourself a fair test on filming style though. Out of your last 11 videos, 10 were talking to camera. You only tried text on screen once. So it's honest to say you haven't really tested different filming styles lately, not that they don't work. There's no matching pair this week where you filmed the same script two different ways, so that kind of proof isn't available yet. For now, the topic you pick seems to move the needle more than the style you shoot it in.

## What is working

Your come-up videos, about how you got started, usually pull about twice your normal views. You've posted 22 of these, so that's a real pattern. Your real money numbers videos do even better, about three and a half times your usual views, across 7 videos. That's a small group but still worth trusting. Videos where you tell people to check your link in bio also do huge numbers, but only 6 of these exist, so treat that as promising, not proven.

## Try this next week

Take a come-up story and film it as text on screen instead of talking to camera, since that style has been quietly outperforming and you've barely tried it. Post another real money numbers video, since that bucket keeps beating your average by a wide margin. Try adding a link in bio call to action onto a come-up video, so you can see if the combo works, not just the CTA alone.

best.md:
This video did really well. It got about 4.8 times the views a normal video of yours gets.

Your opening line was "I launched a company three months ago, and it's already done almost $200,000." That is a strong hook. It stops the scroll and makes people need to know how you did it and what happens next.

After that, you kept giving people reasons to stay. You moved from the money reveal, to people doubting you, to a real moment checking your sales, to a random ice cream and flip flop mishap. That mix of story and real life kept it moving instead of going flat.

You did not have a clear call to action in the video. You could have asked people to comment a word to get something, like tips on how you started, or to follow for more of the story.

Next time, add that comment a word ask earlier, right after the sales reveal, not just in the caption. That is when people are most hooked and most likely to act.

worst.md:
This video did badly. It only got about 2,141 views, well under what a normal video of yours gets.

There was no spoken hook here, just the line "okay but seriously where should we go" as text. That line does not stop the scroll in the first 3 seconds, and it does not make someone need to know what happens next. It reads like a caption, not a hook.

Since this was a photo carousel with no real hook and no story pulling people through, there was likely nothing new keeping people around after the first moment. Nothing here gives someone a reason to stick with it.

There was no call to action on this one. You could have asked people to drop their vacation ideas in the comments, since the whole video is about needing suggestions.

Next time, turn that line into a real spoken hook in the first 3 seconds, something like "I need help picking where to go, tell me now," and then ask for comments early so people have a reason to stay and respond.
